anti_overlap: Does not evaluate how wing bias should mathematically compose with kill-share heredity or playstyle signals in the matcher's scoring — that is fd-loot-bias-composition's remit.

Does not evaluate whether hatch-mapping and loot-farming literacy pull toward different taxonomies, or whether the current Encryptid/RunReport data model can carry a family field — that is fd-dataflow-dual-consumer's remit.
Does not review Beat 2 zone-shaping, mood-gating, or deck/draft integration mechanics, which are out of scope for the wing-set v0 design under review.
decision_lens: Would this taxonomy's boundaries and count survive being run against the real 44-family/645-creature jawnomicon corpus and the felt cadence of one wing-roll per delve, or does it only work as an abstract five-bucket sketch that hasn't been checked against real family sizes, real roster coverage, or real exposure math?
focus: Whether wing-as-tonal-theme is the right classification axis at all, and whether five is the right wing count for Beat-1 literacy, evaluated against the jawnomicon corpus's actual structural family data and genre precedent for player-facing category counts.
name: fd-taxonomy-legibility-design
persona: Apply the perspective of a classification-systems / information-architecture specialist grounded in controlled-vocabulary and faceted-classification practice (apt for a design explicitly framed as archive sections of a Borgesian library), cross-trained on roguelike and ARPG category-bucket design (Path of Exile's gem/item tag taxonomy, Magic's five-color pie, Isaac's floor themes, Slay the Spire's Act structure) — someone who treats a player-facing taxonomy as an artifact that must be internally coherent (each bucket cleanly separable from its neighbors), and whose cardinality is calibrated to the player's actual exposure budget, not to how tidy the bucket count looks on a whiteboard.
review_areas: Taxonomy-axis fit: is 'tonal theme' actually well-supported by the jawnomicon family data, or is it a post-hoc relabeling of structurally-clustered families — the export's own epistemic_note states named families are deterministic Louvain communities over a motif/power 'relatedness' graph, documented resemblance never genealogy, and explicitly orthogonal to the tradition-family axis — meaning a family clustered on shared vocabulary (e.g. 'shy-elusive-avoids-humans', 'large-footprints-left-behind') is not guaranteed to be clustered on shared mood, so a wing built from such families risks internal tonal incoherence even where the family grouping itself is sound.

Corpus coverage of the proposed axis: quantify what fraction of the roster the five straw wings actually reach (the families.json export puts 546 of 645 creatures in a named family at all; the five straw wings' listed families sum to 255 of those 645) and flag any taxonomy whose design leaves a large remainder of the roster permanently unreachable by any wing bias.

Count validity for Beat-1 literacy: is five wings actually calibrated to 'felt often enough to build literacy' given delve-run cadence, or is '3-5' being accepted as self-evidently fine without computing the exposure math (e.g. the coupon-collector expectation for uniform-random wing rolls across n=5 buckets, and how that compares to how often a typical session actually completes a delve)?

Alternative-axis due diligence: does the brainstorm's treatment of the other candidate axes named in the goal (record-type per §11.6, eidogen-dimension-cluster, MediaFeatures region, enemy ecology, player-verb affordance) actually reason about each against real data, or does it wave past them without checking, for instance, what an eidogen-dimension-cluster axis would look like against the 28-axis `dimensions` object on `Encryptid`, or what a MediaFeatures-region axis would look like against `entropy`/`rhythm`/`emotionalTone` in `src/sim/habitat/types.ts`?

Naming/grammar consistency: do the wing names and their constituent-family groupings read as a coherent in-fiction classification scheme (an archive's section headers) rather than an arbitrary post-hoc grouping of unrelated family names chosen for surface tonal resemblance.

Balance and edge cases: the jawnomicon export's family sizes range from 3 to 21 members with confidence ratings from low to high — does the wing design account for the low-confidence or tiny families it pulls in, or name what happens to the 26 families (of 44) the straw proposal excludes entirely?

severity_examples.condition: wing pools are implemented as fixed 1:1 family-to-wing mappings covering only the five straw wings' families, with no catch-all or residual pool for excluded families.
severity_examples.scenario: The wing-set proposal ships as specified, with the five straw wings mapped 1:1 onto their listed jawnomicon families and no residual pool for the rest; roughly 60% of the eventual 645-creature roster (the 26 excluded families plus the ~99 creatures with no family membership at all) can never be favored by any wing roll, permanently starving most of decision 3's promised 'full jawnomicon bestiary' expansion of any legible wing-biased acquisition path.

severity_examples.condition: plan-level open question #1 ('which wings, how many (3-5?)') ships without any exposure-cadence estimate tied to expected delve frequency.
severity_examples.scenario: Five is asserted as the literacy-appropriate wing count without checking it against roll cadence — if wings roll independently and uniformly at random once per delve, a player needs roughly 11 delves in expectation to have seen every wing once (coupon collector, n=5), a number nobody in the design computes or checks against how often the target session actually completes a delve.

severity_examples.condition: no cross-check is shown between a family's rationale/top_shared_vocab fields and the tonal label the wing design assigns to it.
severity_examples.scenario: The wing groupings borrow jawnomicon family names and members directly (e.g. 'Funerary' = Death-Criers + Underworld Court + Night-Comers) without checking that those families, built from motif/power-vocabulary clustering rather than tonal clustering, are actually tonally uniform inside themselves — producing hatches inside a wing that don't reliably read as tonally coherent to the player even though the family-membership mapping is internally consistent.

success_hints: Cites actual family member counts and coverage percentages from families.json (44 families, 546/645 creatures in a named family, the straw five wings covering 255/645) rather than treating the taxonomy question in the abstract.
Computes or estimates the exposure cadence (delves-per-wing-seen) instead of accepting '3-5' as self-justifying.

Engages each of the five alternative axes named in the goal on its own merits using real data (record-type per §11.6, eidogen dimension clusters from `Encryptid.dimensions`, MediaFeatures regions from `types.ts`) rather than a one-line dismissal.

Keeps the taxonomy-axis critique (is tonal-theme right at all) distinct from the within-axis tuning critique (are these five wings well-chosen given tonal-theme is right) rather than conflating the two.
Proposes at least one concretely specified alternative wing set or axis, sized and checked against the same corpus data, not just a directional gesture toward 'maybe fewer wings.'
task_context:
Ideate and evaluate alternatives for the Borgesroom wing-set v0 in After Them — the themed wing identity each delve run rolls, which biases the encryptid matcher's family pools and makes run→creature hatching legible ('this run became this creature'). The current straw proposal is five tonal wings mapped to jawnomicon families: Funerary (Death-Criers/Underworld Court/Night-Comers), Tempest (Tempest-Bringers/Rain-Serpents/Rain-Holders/Maelstrom-Makers), Hearth (Hearth-Bound/Kindly Watchers/Blessing-Bearers/First Teachers), Hungers (Lurking Hunters/Hungers That Think/Monstrous Broods/Wings of Ill Omen), Mirrors (Tricksters/Shape-Thieves/Never-Caught). Evaluate and propose better alternatives on four questions: (1) Is wing-as-tonal-theme the right taxonomy axis at all? Consider alternatives: wings by record type (canon §11.6: 'funerary wings lean funerary records' — wings are archive sections of a Borgesian library), by eidogen dimension cluster, by media-feature region (entropy/rhythm/emotionalTone), by enemy ecology, by player-verb affordance. (2) Is five the right count for Beat 1, given each wing must be felt often enough to build literacy? (3) How should wing bias compose with the other hatch signals (roster kill-share heredity, pace/aggression/thoroughness playstyle axes) so hatches stay legible but not deterministic — and never hard-gate the 645-creature roster? (4) The wings will serve TWO consumers — hatch mapping now, loot-farming literacy later (§11.6) — do the two jobs pull toward different taxonomies, and if so which taxonomy serves both? Ground in the actual sources, do not trust summaries: docs/research/2026-08-09-meta-home-loop-teardowns.md, game-design-docs/teardown-arpg-modifiers.md §11-12, game-design-docs/after-them-delve-formation.md (R1-R8), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/exports/families/v16/families.json (44 families with member lists), /Users/sma/projects/jawnomicon/data/families-prose.yaml (family blurbs), src/sim/habitat/types.ts (MediaFeatures), src/sim/habitat/encryptidMatcher.ts (scoring), src/ui/RunReport.ts (available run facts).
